title: Institutional Retreat From Single-Family
claimText: Institutional buyers are pulling back from single-family acquisitions due to margin compression.
verdictReason: Institutional purchase volume down 34% YoY in February 2026. Invitation Homes and American Homes 4 Rent both reported acquisition slowdowns in Q4 2025 earnings. Rate stability has squeezed spread margins to historical lows.
supportedClaims: Institutional pullback confirmed by transaction data
Margin compression is the primary driver

title: Rates Will Fall Below 5% Within 30 Days
claimText: Mortgage rates will fall below 5% within 30 days due to an imminent Fed pivot.
verdictReason: 30-day period elapsed. Current 30-yr fixed: 6.72%, well above the 5% target. Fed maintained hawkish stance with no pivot signals. Even optimistic projections show 6.2-6.5% as the floor for 2026. Claim fully contradicted by timeline and magnitude.
contradictedClaims: 5% rate target not achievable in timeframe

title: Tech Hub Markets Converting to Buyer's Markets
claimText: SF, Austin, and Seattle will see 6+ months inventory, officially converting to buyer's markets.
verdictReason: Confirmed. SF at 6.8 months, Austin at 7.2 months, Seattle at 6.4 months of inventory as of March 2026. All three metros have crossed the 6-month threshold that defines a buyer's market. Remote work normalization and tech layoffs driving the shift.
supportedClaims: 6+ months inventory confirmed in all three metros

title: Luxury Price Adjustments Accelerating Pre-Spring
claimText: Price adjustments in high-tier markets ($1M+) will accelerate before spring peak season.
verdictReason: Partially confirmed. List price cuts up 28% in the $1M+ segment (Jan-Mar 2026 vs prior year). However, closed sale prices have held within 2% of ask, suggesting negotiation dynamics rather than structural decline. The adjustments are real but may not indicate the deeper correction implied.
supportedClaims: List price reductions accelerating in luxury segment
insufficientDataClaims: Whether this represents structural shift vs seasonal negotiation

title: New Construction Completions Hitting 17-Year High
claimText: New construction completions are at the highest level since 2007, and this wave of supply will push prices down in Sun Belt markets.
verdictReason: FRED data confirms housing completions at 1.52M annualized — highest since Q2 2007. Sun Belt markets (Phoenix, Tampa, Dallas, Atlanta) showing inventory gains of 15-25% YoY, consistent with new supply pressure. Price softening evident in these metros.
insufficientDataClaims: Magnitude of price decline still developing

title: Housing Market Crash of 2026
claimText: The biggest housing crash in history is coming in 2026. Prices will drop 40-50%.
verdictReason: No data supports a 40-50% national price decline. Even the 2008 crash produced a 27% peak-to-trough decline over 5 years. Current fundamentals: unemployment at 4.1%, mortgage delinquency at 3.2% (well below crisis levels), and household formation still exceeding new supply. High fear-mongering language detected.
contradictedClaims: 40-50% price decline has no historical or data-based support
Crash narrative contradicted by employment and delinquency data

title: Commercial Real Estate Distress Spilling Into Residential
claimText: CRE distress, especially in office, is creating a credit tightening that will spill over into residential lending and slow housing activity.
verdictReason: CRE distress is real — office vacancy at 19.8% nationally, regional bank CRE exposure elevated. However, residential lending standards have not materially tightened (Mortgage Credit Availability Index stable). The spillover mechanism exists in theory but hasn't materialized in residential data yet.
supportedClaims: CRE distress is significant and worsening
insufficientDataClaims: Whether credit tightening will eventually materialize

title: Off-Market Deals Getting Easier to Find
claimText: There are more motivated sellers right now than at any point since 2019. Direct-to-seller acquisition has never been easier.
verdictReason: Pre-foreclosure filings up 22% YoY. Expired MLS listings up 31%. Probate filings steady. Days on market increasing means more sellers hitting frustration timelines. Combined with inventory gains, the acquisition environment for direct-to-seller strategies is objectively stronger than any point since pre-COVID.
insufficientDataClaims: Whether 'easiest since 2019' is precisely accurate vs slightly earlier
